definition: to assess the value, quality, or worth of something
memoryTip: APPRAise the price—assess value (not the same as praise).
correctPassage: Before listing the estate, the auction house hired a specialist to appraise the collection of rare maps.
wrongPassages: The audience stood to appraise the conductor after the final chord.
Editors agreed to appraise the manuscript by printing it without review.
She hoped the committee would appraise her proposal with a standing ovation.

definition: to perceive, detect, or recognize with care
memoryTip: DIS-cern: sift carefully until you can tell things apart.
correctPassage: From the blurred satellite image, analysts could still discern the outline of the abandoned runway.
wrongPassages: The firm decided to discern the outdated files by shredding them overnight.
They billed discern as a separate line item on every client invoice.
The supervisor asked staff to discern open tickets by auto-closing anything older than a week.

memoryTip: Con-SPIC-uous: easy to SEE (Latin spicere) because it stands out.
correctPassage: The senator’s bright red scarf made her conspicuous among the gray coats on the steps.
wrongPassages: She kept the signed originals conspicuous in a locked vault no one ever opened.
Once the brass section covered the theme completely, the motif became especially conspicuous.
His muted, camouflaged jacket was chosen to be as conspicuous as possible in the forest.

definition: to formally declare that one is giving something up
memoryTip: Re-NOUNCE: publicly announce you are giving it up.
correctPassage: After the scandal, the heir chose to renounce any claim to the family title.
wrongPassages: Reviewers called the revised statistics renounce once the reanalysis confirmed the findings.
He planned to renounce the award by accepting it on live television.
The empty warehouse looked renounce after decades without tenants or cargo.

definition: a minor weakness or harmless eccentricity
memoryTip: A little FOIBLE is a foil-able flaw—minor, not fatal.
correctPassage: Colleagues forgave his only foible: rearranging every whiteboard marker by color before a meeting.
wrongPassages: Engineers traced the bridge collapse to a single foible in the main support beam.
Investors credited her foible leadership with rescuing the firm during the crisis.
The only foible in the reactor design was the complete absence of a cooling system.
